newsitem.title: USA: Lawmakers urge FCC to reject TV industry's ratings.
newsitem.headline: Lawmakers urge FCC to reject TV industry's ratings.

text.p: A bipartisan group of nearly two dozen congressmen and senators urged the Federal Communications Commission Tuesday to reject the television industry's system for rating programmes.

The age-based ratings, introduced at the start of the year as a part of the 1996 communications law, are to be used in conjunction with a "V-chip" that will allow parents to screen out programmes they consider unsuitable for their children.
Tuesday marked the last day the FCC accepted public comment on the controversial ratings, which include TV-PG for parental guidance suggested and TV-M for mature audiences.

"It is our view that the age-based ratings system propsed by the industry undermines the usefulness of the V-chip to such an extent that the purpose of the statute cannot be fulfilled," said the lawmakers.
They want the ratings to spell out a program's level of sex, violence and foul language.
Among the signatories were Reps. Edward Markey (D-Mass.) and Dan Burton (R-Ind.) and Sens. Joseph Lieberman (D-Conn.) and Dan Coats (R-Ind.).

The FCC is expected to hold public hearings on the matter. The FCC must decide whether or not the industry's ratings system is acceptable. If it finds that it is not, the agency can create an advisory committee to develop a new system.
